paleobiology.what_changes_at_this_node: The series contains only the Holocene node, so there is no sampled predecessor wavelength to difference and no successor. At 95 um the selected mode is a single ocellus (inhibitory halo on the order of the tier scale, full peak-to-peak period longer than the halo). The centimetre brood shell and the shell's ribbing sit at much longer wavelengths and are outside this slot; the CC0 shell photograph is used only as a negative scale control.

equations.kinetics: du/dt = D_u laplacian(u) + gamma (a - u + u^2 v); dv/dt = D_v laplacian(v) + gamma (b - u^2 v)
equations.steady_state: u_s = a + b; v_s = b / (a + b)^2
equations.jacobian: f_u = gamma (-1 + 2 b/(a+b)); f_v = gamma (a+b)^2; g_u = gamma (-2 b/(a+b)); g_v = -gamma (a+b)^2
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.turing_inequality: (D_v f_u + D_u g_v)^2 > 4 D_u D_v det(J) and trace(J) < 0 and det(J) > 0
equations.critical_mode: I(r) = b0 + c exp(-(r/s)^2) + A exp(-(r/(1.4 s))^2) cos(2 pi r / lambda + phi)
equations.landau: dA/dt = sigma A - g A^3, saturated along the critical radial mode
equations.boundary_conditions: Radial profile measured inside the plate, excluding the caption band (y >= 520 px) and a 20 px border. The whole-shell voucher is not a boundary condition for the ocellus PDE.

parameters.note: Chosen for this 95 um Holocene node. Not the sibling slot's alpha_scale 1.39 / beta_offset 0.31.

empirical_claims: Turing (1952) selects a finite critical wavenumber when the inhibitor diffuses farther than the activator and the Jacobian is stable without diffusion.
Gierer & Meinhardt (1972) and Murray (1981) place a spot or ocellus in that wavelength class: local activation, long-range inhibition.
Finn & Norman (2010) show that the female Argonauta argo secretes a thin calcareous brood shell used for buoyancy. They do not publish a 95 um pigment wavelength.

On the vendored 100 um gallery plate the inhibitory-halo radius is measured near 89 um, compared with the 95 um tier label rather than set equal to it. The peak-to-peak period of the same radial mode is longer than the halo.
